title: Prefill Confidence Operationalizer — kernel selection, acceptance curves, and safe fallback
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Implement an operational component that converts prefill probe signals into actionable confidence curves used by the kernel selection and speculative decode routing layers, plus a safe, throttled fallback mechanism when acceptance drops below thresholds. This ticket scopes the runtime-side glue, telemetry, and rollout controls.

Why: Speculative decoding relies on quick prefill probes and acceptance heuristics to choose optimistic model/kernel combinations. Current prototypes produce noisy binary accept/reject decisions that cause oscillations under load and poor tail latency when fallbacks cascade. We need a production-grade operationalizer that smooths signals, maps to kernel affinity choices, and triggers graded fallbacks that preserve SLOs.

Non-goals: model training or changes to model scoring logic, IAM/tenant isolation features, and UI dashboard work (Console work tracked in a follow-up PM ticket).

Success criteria (high level):
- Stable acceptance curves per model+kernel that reduce false accepts by >=40% compared to current binary probe in synthetic workloads.
- End-to-end P95 token latency regression <= +10ms for common request sizes when speculative routing enabled.
- No production-level cascading fallback incidents in canary (monitor-only for 2 weeks)

Deliverables: 
1) Prefill Confidence Operationalizer service (runtime hook): smooths raw probe logits into time-decayed confidence curves per model/kernel, exposes an API consumed by the router.
2) Kernel affinity policy: deterministic mapping from confidence buckets to preferred kernel variants (FP16, Q4, integer quantized) using weighted scoring.
3) Graded fallback controller: three-tier fallback (soft-throttle, route to slower-compatible kernel, full route to conservative model) with hysteresis and cooldown.
4) Telemetry & dashboards: per-key acceptance curve histograms, route-change events, and SLO impact metrics.
5) Integration tests and a canary rollout plan with automated rollback triggers.

Design notes: 
- Confidence curve model: exponential moving average (alpha tunable per model) over acceptance probability from prefill probes plus sequence-length-aware scaling. We will normalize curves to [0,1] and assign buckets: high (>=0.8), medium (>=0.5), low (<0.5).
- Kernel scoring: each kernel gets a score = w_latency * (1 - normalized_latency_rank) + w_cost * (1 - normalized_cost_rank) + w_confidence * confidence; weights are configurable per tenant/project. Kernels with score within 5% of top are considered acceptable to avoid oscillation.
- Fallback policy: on confidence bucket downgrade, first apply soft-throttle (limit concurrency to preserve tail latency), then if sustained for cooldown window, route to a kernel with higher compatibility (e.g., fallback to FP16 fallback kernels), finally fall back to conservative model version if latency or rejection rates exceed thresholds.
- Hysteresis: require two consecutive degradation windows before promoting a harsher fallback.
- Safety: add quota-based circuit breaker to prevent wide blast radius across tenants when fallback logic activates.

Acceptance criteria (detailed):
- Unit tests for curve smoothing, bucketization, and kernel scoring (coverage >= 90% for operationalizer package).
- Integration tests that simulate noisy probe inputs and verify fallback escalation path executes only when thresholds crossed.
- Load tests that validate P95 token latency change <= +10ms under 1x and 3x baseline load when speculative routing enabled.
- Canary: staged rollout to 5% of traffic for 72 hours, then 20% for 5 days. Automatic rollback triggers: +15% P99 latency vs baseline, +2x error rate on specific model endpoints, or sustained increase in token cost >25%.

Telemetry & dashboards: 
- New metrics: prefill_probe_raw_accept_prob (histogram), confidence_curve_value (gauge by model/kernel), route_decision_event (counter with tags), fallback_escalation_event (counter), kernel_switch_latency_impact (histogram).
- Dashboards: Acceptance curves per model, route decision heatmap, fallback incidents timeline.
- Alerts: rate of fallback_escalation_event > threshold, sudden drop in confidence across top models, increasing tail token latency.

Backward compatibility and migration: Router will default to existing binary probe mode unless tenant opts in via runtime flag. The operationalizer exports a compatibility shim that can return binary accept/reject for backward compatibility. We will run both modes in parallel during canary and compare.

Security and privacy: No customer input data is stored long-term; confidence summaries are aggregated. Security review not required for this ticket but will be included if design changes to telemetry require secure storage.

test_plan: 1) Unit tests for smoothing and bucketization. 2) Integration tests with simulated probe noise and kernel permutations. 3) Load tests at 1x and 3x. 4) Canary rollout with automated metrics-based rollback. See perf harness link for scripts.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal canary on staging lanes. Phase 2: 5% traffic canary for 72h. Phase 3: 20% for 5 days. Phase 4: 100% with monitoring. Automatic rollback triggers defined in ticket. Feature gated per-tenant via runtime flag 'spec.operationalizer.enabled'.
telemetry: Emit metrics listed in description. Hook tracing for route_decision_event with tags: model, kernel, confidence_bucket, tenant. Retention: 30d for high-res, 90d aggregated.
open_questions: Optimal alpha for EMA smoothing per model (propose 0.2 initial)
Weights for kernel scoring (latency vs cost vs confidence) — should these be tenant-configurable or centrally tuned?
decisions: Use EMA smoothing with per-model alpha (initial 0.2). Use three confidence buckets with defined hysteresis. Kernel scoring formula will be exposed as tunable flags; default weights: w_latency=0.5, w_cost=0.2, w_confidence=0.3.
recent_updates: 2026-02-20: Spike completed showing EMA smoothing reduces noisy accepts in synthetic workload (doc linked).
2026-02-26: Prototype runtime hook merged to feature branch (PR #1229) — needs refactor to use common metrics client.
2026-03-01: Telemetry schema finalized with SRE; added fallback_escalation_event metric and histogram for kernel_switch_latency_impact.
2026-03-05: Integration test uncovered oscillation when two kernels have near-equal scores; added acceptance rule to prefer previously-running kernel if score delta < 5%.
next_steps: 1) Implement kernel affinity policy module and config flags. 2) Add circuit-breaker and quota-based safety net. 3) Complete integration tests and load tests. 4) Prepare canary and work with SRE to configure alerts and runbooks. 5) Create follow-up PM ticket for Console dashboards (link in description).
followups: PM-428: Console dashboard and runbook for Prefill Confidence Operationalizer
notes: Keep low-level kernel selection logic isolated behind an interface to allow future replacement with model-driven predictors. Track token cost impact carefully when enabling spec routing for high-traffic tenants.
